name: DFRobot Beetle ESP32-C6 Mini Development Board
//sku: DFR1117. Two hardware revisions are sold under it: V1.0 (RT9080 3.3 V LDO, schematic dated 2024-01-17) and V1.1 (TPS62A02DRLR 3.3 V buck, schematic dated 2024-12-06). Everything here is true of both except the regulator, its current and the deep-sleep current, which say which revision they hold for. Which revision the PO's three boards are is NOT known (the back silkscreen prints it, e.g. 'V1.0.0' on DFRobot's pin diagram).
//: Written in walk P735 from DFRobot's wiki, both schematics, DFRobot's own KiCad footprint (layout zip) and the Arduino variant header. One side only: no photo of the boards in hand.
//flash_mb: DFRobot wiki, Specifications: 'Flash: 4MB' (documents.dfr1117-wiki). The schematic's chip is ESP32-C6-FH4 (flash in package).
//wokwi_part_type: Wokwi has no Beetle ESP32-C6. The stand-in is Espressif's ESP32-C6 DevKitC-1; its Wokwi definition was NOT read in this walk, so wokwi_power_pins and documents.wokwi-board are missing.
//physical: DFRobot's own footprint 'Beetle ESP32-C6.kicad_mod' (documents.dfr1117-layout-v1-0, KiCad 8): outline 20.5 x 25 mm with 1.5 mm corner arcs; 16 round through-holes, drill 0.9 mm, pad 1.8 mm, two columns of 8 at 2.54 mm pitch, x = 1.345 and 19.125 (17.78 mm apart), y = -4.56 to -22.34. The dimension drawing (documents.dfr1117-dimension) gives 20.50 x 25.00 mm and puts the USB-C at the y = -25 edge. The footprint is the V1.0 layout; that V1.1 kept it is UNVERIFIED.

physical.//footprint_module: Left out on purpose: DFRobot's footprint is named 'Beetle ESP32-C6' (a space, not a name), and no footprint has been drawn and checked for this board, so --for-fab should refuse it.
physical.//thickness_mm: Not stated in any source read.

header.//first_pad_from_edge_mm: Footprint: the last pad of each column (8 and 9) is at y = -4.56 and the outline edge away from the USB-C at y = 0. From the USB-C edge, pads 1 and 16 sit 25 - 22.34 = 2.66 mm in. Both columns end at the same y, so they are flush at both ends.

physical.//mounting_holes: None: the footprint has no hole but the 16 header pads, the dimension drawing shows none, and the schematic's FD7/FD8 are fiducials.
physical.//buttons: DFRobot's dimension drawing and pin diagram: 'B' left of the USB-C, 'R' right of it, component side up. The wiki: BOOT is IO9. Not checked on a board in hand.

buttons.seen_from: the component side facing you, USB-C at the top

physical.//header_order: Schematic (both revisions): P3 pins 1-8 = GND, 3V3, IO4, IO5, IO23, IO22, IO21, IO7; P4 pins 1-8 = BAT, GND, VUSB, IO17/RX, IO16/TX, IO19, IO20, IO6. DFRobot's KiCad symbol numbers the same pads 1-16 (P3 = 1-8, P4 reversed = 9-16: 9 GPIO6 ... 14 VIN, 15 GND, 16 BAT), and the footprint puts pad 1 and pad 16 at the USB-C end. The silkscreen (dimension drawing) prints 'VIN' for the VUSB net, and bare GPIO numbers for the rest. Each row is listed from the end away from the USB-C, as spark's other boards do. GND1 is P3 pin 1, GND2 is P4 pin 2; the silkscreen prints both as GND.
physical.//pad_aliases: Function names from the Arduino variant (documents.arduino-variant-beetle-c6). The silkscreen prints GPIO numbers only.

//pins: The silkscreen prints the GPIO number itself (dimension drawing, pin diagram). Function names from the Arduino variant header dfrobot_beetle_esp32c6/pins_arduino.h at tag 3.3.12.
//wake_capable_gpio: GPIO0-7 on an ESP32-C6 (LP IO), as the XIAO ESP32-C6 record has it from soc_caps.h (documents.esp-idf-soc-caps-v5-5-1). On this header: 4, 5, 6, 7. GPIO0 is the battery-sense pin, not on the header.
//adc_gpio: GPIO0-6: ESP32-C6 datasheet v1.5 Table 2-8 (page 23), ADC1_CH0-6, as the XIAO record cites it. On this header: 4, 5, 6 (DFRobot's pin diagram: ADC1_4, ADC1_5, ADC1_6).

strapping.note: ESP32-C6 strapping pins (MTMS, MTDI, GPIO8, GPIO9, GPIO15), as the XIAO record cites Espressif's GPIO reference. GPIO4 and GPIO5 are on this header. GPIO8 has a 10K pull-up R11 to 3V3, GPIO9 a 10K pull-up R10 (schematics V1.0 and V1.1). GPIO15 is the LED, held low through it.

console_uart.note: U0TXD, header pad '16', through a 499 R series resistor R7 (schematic). The ROM bootloader prints here on every reset.

onboard_led.note: LED1 'L', lit by a 1: on both schematics GPIO15 drives R16 2.7K into LED1's anode, the cathode on GND. The wiki: 'Onboard LED pin IO15/D13'; the variant: LED_BUILTIN = 15. Not on the header. (The XIAO's LED is lit by a 0; this one is not.)

onboard_button.note: BOOT, silkscreened B, reads 0 when pressed: on both schematics IO9 has the 10K pull-up R10 to 3V3, 1 uF C21 to GND and the switch S1 to GND. The wiki names it 'IO9/D9/BOOT'. Held at reset it enters the bootloader.

divider.source: Schematics V1.0 and V1.1: BAT through R1 1M/1% to IO0, R2 1M/1% to GND, C3 100 nF across R2 (documents.dfr1117-schematics-zip, DFR1117-Schematics-V1.1.pdf, zone D2).

onboard_battery_sense.note: The battery voltage halved, on GPIO0 (ADC1_CH0), from both schematics. The wiki says 'lithium battery charging/monitoring' but names no pin; the schematic does.

usb.note: USB D- (GPIO12) and D+ (GPIO13) through 22 R (R6, R8) to the USB-C (schematic). Driving one drops the USB Serial/JTAG port. Not on the header.

flash.note: The ESP32-C6-FH4's in-package flash, as the XIAO record cites the C6 datasheet v1.5 (Table 2-4, page 20). Not on the header.

i2c.note: SDA 19, SCL 20 (variant header; the wiki pin diagram agrees). No I2C pull-ups on the board (schematic).

//deep_sleep: The ESP32-C6's wake API under MicroPython, as the XIAO record holds it (same chip): wake_on_ext0 does not exist on the C6.

charger.source: Schematics V1.0 and V1.1: U7 TP4057, VCC from VUSB, BAT to the BAT net; the wiki: 'TP4057 lithium battery charge management chip'.

charge_current_a.source: DFRobot wiki, Specifications: 'Max charging current: 0.5A'. The schematic sets PROG with R20 2K.

regulator.value: V1.1: TPS62A02DRLR 3.3 V buck; V1.0: RT9080 3.3 V LDO
regulator.source: Schematic V1.1 U1 TPS62A02DRLR, schematic V1.0 U1 RT9080; the wiki: 'V1.0: RT9080 3.3V LDO V1.1: TPS62A02DRLR 3.3V DC-DC'.

regulator_3v3_a.source: The lower of the two revisions: RT9080 'up to 600mA of output current' (RT9080 datasheet page 1, in documents.dfr1117-datasheet-zip); TPS62A02 IOUT 0-2 A (TPS62A02DRLR datasheet, 7.3 Recommended Operating Conditions, page 4, same zip).
regulator_3v3_a.why_it_matters: What everything on 3V3 is summed against. 0.6 A holds for V1.0; a V1.1 board gives 2 A. Read the revision off the back of the PO's boards.

module_peak_a.source: ESP32-C6 Series Datasheet v1.5, Table 5-7 (page 66): 802.11b 1 Mbps @ 21.0 dBm TX, 354 mA peak, the bare chip's figure; the citation the XIAO record holds, reused.

deep_sleep_ua.source: DFRobot wiki, Specifications: 'Sleep Current (Deep Sleep Mode, Battery-Powered) Version 1.0: 14μA Version 1.1: 37μA'. The higher one is held.
deep_sleep_ua.why_it_matters: The battery life of the project. 14 uA on V1.0, 37 uA on V1.1; the PO's revision is unknown.

internal_pull_up_ohms.source: ESP32-C6 Series Datasheet v1.5, DC characteristics (page 65): RPU 45 kOhm typical; the XIAO record's citation, reused.

io_volts.source: DFRobot wiki: 'Operating voltage: 3.3V'; the regulator makes 3V3 (schematic).

battery_input.value: header pads, no connector: BAT (right row, pad 16, at the USB-C end) and GND beside it (pad 15)
battery_input.source: Schematics: P4 pin 1 BAT, pin 2 GND; the footprint and DFRobot's symbol: pad 16 BAT, pad 15 GND; the board drawing shows no battery connector.

//power_pads: VIN is the VUSB net itself (schematic P4 pin 3 = VUSB): with USB plugged in it carries the USB 5 V, and a supply on VIN meets the USB host's VBUS with no diode between them. VUSB reaches the regulator through the Schottky D3 1N5819W; BAT reaches it through the P-FET Q1 AO3407, which turns off when VUSB is present (R17 10K gate pull-down).
